purpose: Static research map. Candidate keywords and reading recommendations are hypotheses inferred from the three seed papers, not an exhaustive literature review.

seed_papers.title: RefAlign: Representation Alignment for Reference-to-Video Generation
OmniVBench: A Benchmark and Large-Scale Dataset for Omni Reference-to-Video Generation

recommended_papers.title: Identity-Consistent Video Generation under Large Facial-Angle Variations (Mv²ID)
recommended_papers.why: Adds multi-view identity, view-dependent copy-paste, and motion naturalness to the seed themes.

recommended_papers.title: HarmoView: Harmonizing Multi-View Constraints for Identity-Consistent Video Generation
recommended_papers.why: Explore view fusion, reference-view mismatch, identity crosstalk, and staged training.

recommended_papers.title: Aura: Consistent Multi-Subject Video Generation via VLM-Grounded Semantic Alignment
recommended_papers.why: Connect representation alignment to multi-subject interactions, VLM grounding, subject-aware encoding, and prompt alignment.

recommended_papers.title: KeyID: Decoupled Drafting and Keyframe Editing for Identity-Preserving Video Generation
recommended_papers.why: Explore a training-free alternative separating motion drafting from identity correction.

recommended_papers.title: Kaleido: Open-Sourced Multi-Subject Reference Video Generation Model
recommended_papers.why: Implementation-oriented follow-up on open-source subject-to-video, multi-image conditioning, background disentanglement, and data construction.

recommended_papers.title: MV-S2V: Multi-View Subject-Consistent Video Generation
recommended_papers.why: Extends single-view subject-to-video toward multi-view and 3D-level consistency.

recommended_papers.title: Spatial-Temporal Decoupled Reference Conditioning for Identity-Preserving Text-to-Video Generation
recommended_papers.why: Investigate spatial/temporal separation in reference conditioning and positional encoding.

keywords.question: How is identity preserved across frames, viewpoints, and long sequences?
Do multiple reference views improve identity without copy-paste artifacts?
How are different reference images assigned to factors or subjects?
How do we distinguish genuine generation from copying reference pixels?
Which representation spaces and alignment losses improve fidelity and controllability?
Can each requested factor be scored independently and attributed to the right subject?
How can prompt adherence be balanced against reference fidelity?
How are identities, actions, and interactions separated across subjects?
Does identity preservation compromise realistic motion?
Which paired, cross-paired, synthetic, or video-text data is necessary?
Can vision-language features ground identity and semantic relationships?
How can positional encoding separate reference tokens from video tokens or subjects?
Can identity be injected or corrected without additional training?
Can sparse identity corrections preserve motion over long sequences?
Which protocols expose failure modes missed by aggregate scores?
How does data scale and diversity affect zero-shot reference conditioning?
Can subject identity be separated from background and scene?
Does the correct identity receive the correct action and attributes?
How consistent is a subject across views and implicit 3D structure?
Should spatial identity cues and temporal motion cues be conditioned separately?
How can instruction following be measured alongside identity fidelity?
Can synthetic data reduce the cost of multi-view training sets?
Does staged training stabilize transitions from T2V to multi-view control?
When do multiple subjects leak features or identities into one another?
